title: Friendly to all
hookLine: Krishna: dear to me is one who hates no being, friendly and compassionate (Bhagavad Gita 12.13)
carry: a stranger at a bus stop

cards: A battlefield, two armies facing each other, and in the space between them a chariot. The warrior Arjuna has lost his nerve, and his charioteer, Krishna, is talking him through it. That conversation is the Bhagavad Gita.

By its twelfth chapter, Arjuna has seen a vision of Krishna's cosmic form, and now he asks a quieter question: who knows yoga better, those who worship Krishna in a form, or those who worship the formless?
Krishna's answer winds toward a portrait of a person. And the portrait starts with one who hates no being.

teach.b: Krishna says, in paraphrase: the one who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from the sense of mine and free from ego, the same in pain and pleasure, and forgiving, that devotee is dear to me.
Notice where it starts. Not with prayer or sacrifice: with hating no one.
The word for friendly, in Sanskrit, is maitra. Not friends with all, as if everyone becomes your best friend. Friendly: a basic warmth toward every being, the default setting of the heart.
Right beside it stands compassion, karuna, which feels for those who suffer. The same verse joins friendliness to letting go of possessiveness and ego.
Some readers hear a link there: unfriendliness can grow out of mine. My seat, my way, my turn. When the grip on mine loosens, there's more room to be friendly.
And then, dear to God. Earlier in the Gita, Krishna speaks of devotion as offering.
Here he says who is dear to him: the person whose love has spilled outward into how they treat every creature. Devotion to God, in this verse, shows up as friendliness to everyone else.
A stranger at a bus stop becomes part of the practice.

how: Hindus read and recite the Bhagavad Gita at home, in temples and in study groups, and its twelfth chapter, on devotion, is sometimes recited on its own.

o: friendly: a basic warmth toward every being
a best friend you share everything with
a polite greeting said to an elder

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.

games.q: Krishna paints a portrait of the devotee dear to him. what comes first in it?
o: one who performs the most sacrifices.
one who hates no being, friendly and compassionate.
one who knows the most scripture.
games.why: his portrait begins with hating no being: friendliness and compassion, freedom from mine.

practice: Picture a stranger you saw recently, someone in line, a driver, a person walking a dog, whose name and story you don't know.
Let yourself be friendly toward them, not loving, not attached, just warm, the way you'd nod at a neighbor, and picture the nod you'd give if you passed them again tomorrow.
If you pray, you can hold them in your own tradition's words.

wordCard.voice: Maitra. The Sanskrit word for a basic warmth toward every being, the devotee's friendliness that Krishna calls dear to him. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: friendly, the word in Gita 12.13, set beside karuṇa, compassionate.
